metadata.description: Wire format for `vibe artifacts where [<package>] --json` (`vibe-artifacts-where/1`, PROP-066 `#drops`): where a person puts the vibe releases and the package payloads a closed network cannot download, and whether the declared bytes are already there. Source of truth for `crates/vibe-wire/src/generated/artifacts_where_report/mod.rs`.
Where one release of this platform goes, for the effective release source.
The `[artifacts] packages` drop directory, or `null` when no drop is configured.

Every downloaded input of every installer option of the package named on the command line; `[]` when no package was named or the package downloads nothing. Required member: an absent key would make the document invalid by this same schema (rule R21).
The effective release source and, when it is a drop or a raw repository, the directory one release goes into.
The directory, repository or base URL releases are read from.
Which input decided the source — `built-in default`, `$VIBEVM_RELEASE_ORIGIN`, `[self] in <file>` or `[artifacts] vibe in <file>`.
The directory the running version's release goes into, for a `localdir` or `nexus` source; `null` when releases are downloaded from the source instead.
The files that directory must hold for this machine; `[]` when there is no drop to fill. Required member: an absent key would make the document invalid by this same schema (rule R21).
One downloaded input of one installer option: the places the drop is searched, in order, and what was found there.
The input's name (a `sources` input) or the step's id (an `archive` / `native` source).
The portable file name the drop is searched for — the URL's last path segment, or an author-side `drop` input's `file`; `null` when neither names one.
The declared digest, lower-case hex; always verified before a dropped file is used.
The declared origin URL, or `null` for an author-side drop input.
The drop paths looked at, highest first; `[]` when no drop is configured. Required member: an absent key would make the document invalid by this same schema (rule R21).

`present`: a searched path holds the declared bytes; `mismatch`: the first file found holds other bytes; `missing`: no searched path holds a file; `no-drop`: nothing was searched because no `[artifacts] packages` drop is configured. Closed: automation decides from it whether an operator still has files to copy.
